substeps.label: C2 · bandsaw: track block out (1/2)
substeps.caption: Rough cuts on the bandsaw (bi-metal blade, coolant for stainless). Panel A lies flat, tracks up, and two cuts along the tracks' rows take off the sides, leaving a strip with the 25 mm track block in the middle.

substeps.label: C2 · bandsaw: track block out (2/2)
substeps.caption: Then the strip turns and two cross-cuts free the block. The panel's ID went with the offcuts, so scribe it again on the block. Every bandsaw cut stays clear of the tracks; the section plane is far from these faces.

substeps.label: C2 · bandsaw: slab off
substeps.caption: Next the block goes on its side and the top 7 mm slab, which holds the tracks, comes off. The rest of the block is scrap, like the rest of the panel (option A).

substeps.label: C2 · bandsaw: one slab per row
substeps.caption: Then the slab lies flat and is split between the two rows: one slab per row of nine tracks. A bandsaw face is rough and deformed, so every bandsaw cut stays at least 1–2 mm from the target plane.

substeps.label: C2 · final face on the precision saw
substeps.caption: Final face on an abrasive cut-off saw or a low-speed precision saw with coolant (MIT used an IsoMet 4000 at 4000 rpm, 6 mm/min), 1.5 mm past the tracks' mid-length. Row 2 waits its turn.
